severities.P0: App cannot load, mission cannot complete, hidden-truth leak, data corruption, or official result mismatch.
severities.P1: Serious incorrect behavior, major scientific misrepresentation, major accessibility blocker, or reproducibility failure.
severities.P2: Significant workflow, usability, teaching, benchmark, or performance gap.

categories.SCI: Scientific model, assumption, evidence, unit, or validation concern.
categories.EDU: Teaching, onboarding, explanation, terminology, or misconception concern.
categories.BENCH: Benchmark artifact, fairness, notebook, solver packet, import/export, reproducibility, timing, or result-parity concern.
categories.UX: User interaction, navigation, discoverability, layout, or workflow friction.
categories.OPS: Pilot operations, feedback intake, checklist, release, or support process.
categories.PERF: Rendering, boot, frame timing, memory, or resource lifecycle.
categories.ACCESS: Keyboard, focus, contrast, semantics, reduced motion, or screen-reader issue.

items.title: Environment Studio domain, resolution, tile bathymetry, editable terrain
items.summary: Alpha testers want a unified editor for defining spatial domain size, resolution, bathymetry generation, regional bathymetry tiles, editable or deformed terrain, and import/export.
items.decision: Accepted for ENV-STUDIO-R0 architecture and contracts.
acceptanceCriteria: Environment-authoring requirements are tracked without adding a fifth Product Hub pillar.
Contracts remain separate from simulation, scoring, and scientific-model changes.
Future visible editor work can reference one stable feedback item.

items.title: Researcher Notebook Launchpad from inside ANCHOR
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / External Solver Evaluation / Researcher Quick Start
items.summary: Alpha testers are unsure whether they must download the full source project and upload the notebook manually. ANCHOR should provide an in-app launch and download page for the external solver notebooks and benchmark bundle.
acceptanceCriteria: Researcher Quick Start exposes the full notebook, starter notebook, public bundle, and finalizer command.
The app states that users do not need the full source repository for normal Alpha use.
The hosted Colab button is enabled only when a public GitHub notebook URL is configured.

items.title: Hosted Google Colab smoke pending
items.summary: Local Python notebook execution and authoritative ANCHOR finalization are verified, but a real hosted Google Colab Run All smoke remains pending.
items.decision: Track separately from local notebook verification.
acceptanceCriteria: Hosted Google Colab status remains PENDING until a real hosted run is completed.
Documentation distinguishes local Python verification from hosted Colab verification.
No release surface claims hosted Colab verification without evidence.

items.title: Feedback and diagnostic package taxonomy
items.summary: Alpha feedback should be categorized consistently as P0/P1/P2/P3 and SCI, EDU, BENCH, OPS, UX, PERF, or ACCESS.
items.decision: Use feedback ledger as the source of truth.
acceptanceCriteria: Feedback IDs are stable and parseable.
Statuses and category tags are auditable.
P0/P1 items cannot be silently marked ignored.

items.title: Environment Studio needs regional 3D bathymetry authoring, not flat 2D tile swatches.
items.summary: Alpha review found that the R1 editor still appears like a flat 2D tile board and is too dominated by localized shore/shelf tiles. Users want to author larger mission-scale synthetic regions, including gulf-like basins, shelves, canyons, islands, seamounts, river-mouth zones, ridges, sills, and deep-water mission opportunities suitable for multiple gliders.
items.decision: Accepted for ENV-STUDIO-R1.1 regional input model, 3D preview, contextual inspector, and multi-archetype regional generator controls.
acceptanceCriteria: Environment Studio remains one unified editor under Simulation Lab.
Regional bathymetry authoring exposes 3D preview, source-grid versus preview-mesh metadata, and multi-archetype provenance.
The phase does not change simulation, scoring, current generation, scalar generation, benchmark fairness, or Product Hub pillars.

items.title: Environment Studio should start from a Synthetic Ocean Atlas and operational window selection.
items.summary: Alpha review found that mission authors think in terms of operational areas, not low-level terrain-feature controls. Environment Studio should present a simplified synthetic world/ocean atlas where users draw an operational window near coast, gulf, island, strait, shelf break, deep basin, river mouth, or open ocean regions. The selected window should infer a regional mission recipe that drives bathymetry, current/scalar regimes, mission scale, glider count, and validation.
acceptanceCriteria: Environment Studio opens to a Synthetic Ocean Atlas stage before feature/tile tuning.
Operational window selection records detected regional context and mission recipe metadata.
Feature and source-tile controls remain available as advanced provenance after regional generation.

items.title: Synthetic Ocean Atlas needs a procedural field engine and window-conditioned bathymetry generator.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Synthetic Ocean Atlas
items.summary: The current atlas is too symbolic. Alpha review wants a seeded synthetic world map whose environmental fields determine land masses, coastline context, shelf/basin/island/gulf regimes, current/scalar regime hints, and generated regional bathymetry from a selected operational window.
acceptanceCriteria: Atlas generation is deterministic, procedural, field-based, and not a real Earth map.
Operational window inference samples atlas fields and produces a Regional Mission Recipe.
Generated bathymetry comes from structured procedural features, distance fields, seeded placement, controlled roughness, validation, and provenance.

items.title: Synthetic Ocean Atlas should regenerate package-backed current, scalar, and hotspot artifacts.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Field Regeneration
items.summary: After regional bathymetry generation, Environment Studio should be able to regenerate deterministic synthetic CurrentField4D, ScalarField4D, hotspot candidates, and field diagnostics from atlas context, bathymetry, masks, coastline, open boundaries, feature zones, and regime hints.
items.decision: Accepted for FIELD-REGEN-R1 as a package-backed synthetic regeneration pass. It does not launch missions from Studio projects, change simulation, change scoring, claim calibrated ocean products, or create operational forecasts.
acceptanceCriteria: Current regeneration uses packages/currents and a reduced-order bathymetry/atlas-conditioned synthetic backend.
Scalar and hotspot regeneration uses packages/scalar-processes when package adapters are available.
Generated metadata records digests, components, diagnostics, dependency states, and claim boundaries.
Starts/drop zones remain NEEDS_VALIDATION and benchmark bundles remain REQUIRES_REGENERATION.
No exported public artifact claims HYCOM, Marine Copernicus, calibrated ocean forecasts, operational forecasts, hidden truth, simulation changes, or scoring changes.

items.title: Environment Studio should be reauthored around a procedural synthetic world map and user-drawn operational boundary.
items.summary: Current Environment Studio remains too parameter-heavy and symbolic. Alpha review wants a generated high-resolution synthetic world map with land masses, islands, oceans, and coarse flow-regime context. Users should pan/zoom the world map, define their own operational boundary box, and then generate regional 3D bathymetry from that selected window.
acceptanceCriteria: Environment Studio opens to a deterministic synthetic world-map artifact.
Users select an operational boundary window that samples world fields.
Selected windows drive regional 3D bathymetry generation while mission planning, scoring, current/scalar equations, and launch workflows remain unchanged.

items.title: Environment Studio must use a real pan/zoom procedural synthetic world map, not pixel-grid atlas art.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Synthetic World Map
items.summary: Alpha review found that the Environment Studio world map still appears as static pixel-grid art with a heavy control panel. Users want to generate a large synthetic Earth-like ocean world with land masses, islands, oceans, and coarse environmental fields; pan and zoom around it; select their own operational boundary; and then generate regional 3D bathymetry from that selected window.
acceptanceCriteria: Environment Studio opens to a large generated synthetic world-map viewport rather than a symbolic atlas diagram.
Users can pan, zoom, choose broad generation controls, and drag an operational boundary window.
Selected windows sample deterministic synthetic world fields and drive regional 3D bathymetry generation without changing mission simulation, scoring, planners, or current/scalar equations.

items.title: Environment Studio needs hard visual acceptance for a world-map-first workflow.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Synthetic World Map
items.summary: Alpha review found that the Environment Studio world-map pass still risked reading like a symbolic local atlas or schematic tile board. The workflow needs a hard browser visual acceptance package proving that Stage 1 opens on a large procedural synthetic world map with pan/zoom, layers, a selected operational boundary, and regional bathymetry generated from that boundary.
items.decision: Accepted for ENV-WORLD-R1A as a visual acceptance and workflow hardening pass. It does not change mission simulation, scoring, planner behavior, current/scalar generation equations, benchmark fairness, or existing Alpha workflows.
acceptanceCriteria: Environment Studio Stage 1 default is a Synthetic World Map viewport, not a symbolic atlas diagram or DOM cell grid.
Owner-review screenshots capture default, panned, zoomed, bathymetry-layer, flow-layer, selected-boundary, and generated-regional-bathymetry states.

The QA summary records world/window digests, pan/zoom evidence, visible land/island/open-ocean metrics, selected-window area, forbidden Stage 1 control count, hidden-truth status, and unchanged simulation/scoring flags.
The selected operational window remains a small regional subset of the synthetic world and drives regional 3D bathymetry generation.

items.title: Flat synthetic world-map UI rejected; Environment Studio needs high-resolution synthetic globe selector.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Synthetic Globe Selector
items.summary: Alpha review rejected the low-resolution local flat-map mental model. Environment Studio Stage 1 should generate a deterministic high-resolution equirectangular synthetic world-field artifact, render it as the primary interactive globe selector, let users select a small operational globe region, and generate regional 2.5D bathymetry from that selected context.
items.decision: Accepted for ENV-GLOBE-R1 as a front-door reauthoring pass. The globe is the selector, the equirectangular fields are the canonical generated artifact, and regional bathymetry is the output. Currents, scalars, hotspots, launch-to-planning, simulation, scoring, planner behavior, and benchmark fairness remain unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: Environment Studio Stage 1 default is a visible interactive globe, not a flat rectangle or pixel-grid map.
The first artifact is `anchor.synthetic-globe-world` with canonical equirectangular resolution at least 2048 x 1024 and default 4096 x 2048.
Users can rotate and zoom the globe, inspect synthetic layers, and select a small operational region below 5 percent of the globe.
Selected regions produce `anchor.operational-globe-window` context and can generate regional 3D bathymetry through the existing builder.
Owner-review screenshots and QA summary are written under `test-results/env-globe-r1-owner-review/`.

No exported public artifact claims real Earth, GEBCO, ETOPO, HYCOM, Copernicus, calibrated survey data, operational forecast, certified navigation, hidden truth, simulation changes, or scoring changes.

items.title: Environment Studio should start from a reference bathymetry atlas and user-selected real patch.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Reference Bathymetry Atlas
items.summary: Alpha review clarified that the issue is not 2D versus globe; the active front door should be a reference bathymetry atlas with lon/lat bounding-box selection and regional patch extraction. Procedural world and globe workflows should be demoted to an experimental sandbox.
items.decision: Accepted for REAL-BATHY-R1 as a production-path correction. The workflow is reference bathymetry atlas -> bounding box -> extracted patch -> regional 3D bathymetry. If no preprocessed public GEBCO/ETOPO fixture is checked in, the browser must show an explicit NO_REFERENCE_DATA_FIXTURE placeholder and must not claim real-data completion.
acceptanceCriteria: Environment Studio defaults to Reference Bathymetry Atlas, not procedural synthetic world or globe.
Users can pan/zoom the reference atlas, select a lon/lat bounding box, inspect selected patch metadata, and generate regional 3D bathymetry from the selected patch.
Procedural synthetic world/globe remains reachable only as an experimental sandbox or compatibility path.
Owner-review screenshots and QA summary are written under `test-results/real-bathy-r1-owner-review/`.
Exports preserve reference dataset identity, atlas digest, selected patch digest, bathymetry artifact digest, validation status, and deferred current/scalar/hotspot dependencies.
If no public reference fixture exists, artifacts and docs clearly report `REAL_BATHY_R1_BLOCKED_WAITING_FOR_REFERENCE_FIXTURE` and `NO_REFERENCE_DATA_FIXTURE`.
Mission simulation, official scoring, planners, glider dynamics, current/scalar generation, and benchmark fairness remain unchanged.

items.title: Reference bathymetry patch needs coupled environment field generation.
items.affectedWorkflow: Simulation Lab / Environment Studio / Reference Bathymetry Field Generation
items.summary: ANCHOR now has a verified 15 arc-second Monterey Canyon reference bathymetry patch. To become a usable mission environment, Environment Studio must generate bathymetry-conditioned synthetic currents, scalar fields, hotspots, candidate starts/drop zones, hazards, and an EnvironmentArtifact from that reference patch.
acceptanceCriteria: Reference bathymetry generates deterministic synthetic current, scalar, hotspot, start/drop-zone, and hazard metadata.
Exports preserve reference fixture identity, field digests, dependency states, validation report, provenance, and claim boundaries.
Currents and scalars are labeled as synthetic bathymetry-conditioned benchmark fields, not operational forecasts.
Mission simulation, scoring, planners, glider dynamics, and benchmark fairness remain unchanged.
